gap: No result ChatGPT got states, in one table, where each station's "3,000 W" can actually be drawn: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus has four 20 A sockets (2,400 W each at 120 V) and no 30 A outlet, DJI rates the Power 2000 at 25 A in total and 12 A (1,440 W) in bypass, BLUETTI's Apex 200 gives 3,200 W on its own and 3,600 W only with an expansion battery or AC/solar input, and Anker's F3000 passes 3,600 W through one TT-30R.
standout_why: Rivals and ChatGPT already hold parts of it. ChatGPT's second answer says the EcoFlow's 3,000 W is shared across outlets rated 20 A each, from the cited manual. outagehouse.com (in the results, not cited) gives per-outlet and grid-on limits for the Jackery HomePower 3000 (2,400 W per household outlet, 3,600 W from the 30 A outlet, 1,440 W with the grid on) but does not cover the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus, DJI Power 2000, Anker F3000 or Apex 200. rvgearlab (cited), powerstationsrated (cited) and wattsift (cited) state no per-outlet limit, no bypass limit and no cycle end-of-life percentage; wattsift marks TT-30 on the F3000 and DELTA 3 Ultra as 'not confirmed'. truewattlab (cited) has 4,000 cycles to at least 80% for the DELTA 3 Max Plus and powerstations.reviews (cited) has 4,000 cycles to 70% for the HomePower 3000, but neither sets the two yardsticks side by side. New against all of them: DJI's 25 A / 12 A bypass figures, the Apex 200's 3,200 W-alone condition, and StorageReview's measured 1.64 kWh (80%) from the DELTA 3 Max Plus, where truewattlab and ChatGPT assume 85%.
decides: It confirms the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus only for loads split across sockets (for example a heater and a microwave on separate outlets); it cannot put more than 2,400 W through one plug and has no 30 A RV outlet. For a 30 A RV or any single load above 2,400 W the pick moves to a unit with a TT-30R: the Anker F3000 (3,600 W on the TT-30R, but sold out with a 3–7 week ship notice), the Jackery HomePower 3000 (3,600 W from its 30 A outlet per outagehouse) or the BLUETTI Apex 200 (TT-30R, but 3,200 W alone and shipping from mid-February 2027, so it cannot be the pick). StorageReview's measurement trims ChatGPT's 35-minute runtime at 3,000 W for the EcoFlow to about 33 minutes. I could not open the ALLPOWERS R3500 page, so whether ours places on these terms is still open.

findings.label: AC output as EcoFlow states it, and the per-socket limit
findings.value: 3,000 W total (6,000 W surge) at 120 V across 4 AC ports, each 20 A max; no 30 A / TT-30 outlet listed
findings.note: Arithmetic: 20 A × 120 V = 2,400 W from any one socket; 3,000 W needs two or more sockets. EcoFlow's page gives amps per port, not watts.

findings.label: Port list (named reviewer)
findings.value: Four NEMA 5-20R outlets at 120 V / 20 A; no TT-30R. The DELTA 3 Ultra Plus adds one NEMA TT-30R at 120 V / 30 A.
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus & Ultra Plus Review (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty, 2025-09-30)
findings.note: Confirms EcoFlow's spec page: the Max Plus has no 30 A outlet.

findings.label: X-Boost figure (not continuous output)
findings.value: 3,800 W X-Boost against 3,000 W rated; the DELTA 3 Max is 2,400 W rated with 3,400 W X-Boost
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus Portable Power Station (2048Wh), EcoFlow US store
findings.note: The DELTA 3 Max ($879 on the store today) is a '3,400 W' listing that falls short of the 3,000 W continuous line: its rated output is 2,400 W. rvgearlab describes X-Boost as 'up to 3,800W for resistive loads'.

findings.label: Measured usable AC energy (named reviewer)
findings.value: 1.64 kWh discharged, 80% of the rated 2,048 Wh; UPS transfer measured at 8 ms
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus & Ultra Plus Review (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty, 2025-09-30)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 1,640 Wh ÷ 3,000 W = 0.55 h, about 33 min at full load, against ChatGPT's 35 min from an assumed 85%. StorageReview published no sustained 3,000 W test, so the 33 min is a calculation. The same review measured the DELTA 3 Ultra Plus at 2.61 kWh (85% of 3,072 Wh).

findings.label: Price, weight, charging, warranty
findings.value: $1,149.00 (compare-at $3,399.00), in stock; 22.1 ± 0.4 kg (48.7 lb); 1,800 W AC input; 1,000 W solar; UPS under 10 ms; 3-year warranty plus 2 years on app registration
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus Portable Power Station (2048Wh), EcoFlow US store
findings.note: Price via storecheck on the EcoFlow US store. Weight, inputs and warranty are from https://www.ecoflow.com/us/delta-3-max-plus-portable-power-station/specs, read the same day; the lb figure is StorageReview's conversion. The same store search showed the DELTA 3 Ultra Plus at $1,599 and the DELTA 3800 Gen4 (3,600 W continuous) at $1,699; no 'Delta 3000 Gen4' at $1,299 appeared.

findings.label: Cycle life yardstick
findings.source_title: 2026 Portable Power Station Spec Database & Real $/Useful Wh Index, TrueWattLab
findings.note: Third-party database, and a cited rival. EcoFlow's own spec page lists no cycle figure. TrueWattLab's usable figure of about 1,741 Wh is a default 85% assumption it marks as not verified.

findings.label: AC output as DJI states it (US model DYM2000L)
findings.value: AC 100–120 V, 25 A total across 4 AC outputs; in bypass mode AC 100–120 V, 12 A
findings.note: DJI's spec page gives amps, not watts. Arithmetic: 25 A × 120 V = 3,000 W on battery; 12 A × 120 V = 1,440 W passed through when plugged into the wall. Per-outlet limit and outlet type are not listed; no TT-30 is mentioned.

findings.label: Cycle life yardstick and test condition
findings.value: Over 80% capacity after 4,000 cycles, tested at 25 °C, Standard Mode recharge, discharged at 2,000 W; 2,048 Wh; about 22 kg; power supply range −10 to 45 °C
findings.note: The cycle test discharges at 2,000 W, not at the 3,000 W rating. 22 kg × 2.2046 = about 48.5 lb, which matches powerstationsrated's figure.

findings.label: Per-outlet ratings as Anker states them
findings.value: NEMA 5-20R: 120 V, 20 A max, 2,400 W max per outlet, 3,600 W total; TT-30R: 120 V, 30 A max, 3,600 W max; AC surge 7,200 W; SurgePad 4,860 W
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3000 Portable Power Station, Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: The full 3,600 W is available from one socket, the TT-30R. SurgePad is a boost figure, not continuous output.

findings.label: Availability, cycle claim, weight, charging
findings.value: Sold out ('Price Loading'); 'all F3000 orders will ship within 3–7 weeks'; '4000 Cycles' with no end-of-life percentage; 3,072 Wh LFP; 91.5 lb; 2,400 W solar (1,600 W + 800 W); 1,800 W AC on a 15 A cable (under 3 hours) or 3,600 W via TT-30; UPS 20 ms
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3000 Portable Power Station, Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: No price was shown on Anker's page today, so ChatGPT's $1,499.99 (Micro Center) and the research lead's $1,699.99 could not be checked there. With a ship time that can exceed four weeks, it cannot be the pick while other rows ship sooner.

findings.label: Continuous output and its condition
findings.value: 3,200 W continuous on its own; up to 3,600 W only 'with a compatible expansion battery or under supported AC or solar input conditions'; 5,400 W Lifting Power; TT-30R outlet; UPS ≤15 ms
findings.source_title: Apex 200 Versatile Power Station, BLUETTI US
findings.note: The table figure for one unit on battery is 3,200 W, not the 3,600 W in BLUETTI's bundle headlines. The page text read does not say which loads Lifting Power covers or give the TT-30R's watt rating.

findings.label: Cycle life yardstick, price, ship date
findings.value: Cycle figures are 'based on BLUETTI laboratory testing to 70% of original battery capacity'; $1,149.00 (compare-at $1,399.00); orders placed on or after Nov. 25 ship starting mid-February
findings.source_title: Apex 200 Versatile Power Station, BLUETTI US
findings.note: Price via storecheck search on bluettipower.com the same day. BLUETTI counts cycles to 70% where DJI counts to 80% (and TrueWattLab gives 80% for EcoFlow), so the counts are not like for like. Shipping is more than four weeks out.

findings.label: Per-outlet, grid-on and cold limits (third-party page)
findings.value: 3,600 W continuous, 7,200 W surge; 2,400 W per household outlet; 3,600 W from the 30 A outlet; 1,440 W output limit with the grid on; 2,000 W limit between 5 and 14 °F; 59.52 lb
findings.source_title: 3,000 W Portable Power Stations for Home Backup Compared, Outage House (2026-11-11)
findings.note: Jackery's own product page returned HTTP 429 on three tries today, so these are Outage House's figures, not read from Jackery. This page was in ChatGPT's results (not cited), so this row is not new.

findings.label: Cycle life yardstick (third-party page)
findings.value: 4,000 cycles to 70%; LiFePO4; 3,072 Wh; $1,499 at Jackery as checked by that site on 2026-11-03
findings.source_title: Jackery 3000: the 3000 Pro, the HomePower 3000, and which to buy, powerstations.reviews
findings.note: Cited rival. The $1,499 is that site's Nov 3 reading, not today's price; ChatGPT showed $1,199 at Walmart. The Explorer 3000 Pro on the same page is NMC, 2,000 cycles to 70%, and discontinued.

findings.label: Why one 120 V household socket cannot carry 3,000 W
findings.value: A 20 A socket at 120 V carries 2,400 W; a 30 A TT-30R carries 3,600 W
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3000 Portable Power Station, Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Anker states both figures for its own outlets; the same arithmetic (amps × 120 V) applies to EcoFlow's 20 A ports. A '3,000 W' station without a 30 A outlet delivers its rating only as a sum across sockets.

findings.label: What the cited rival pages do not state
findings.value: rvgearlab, powerstationsrated and wattsift give no per-outlet limit, no bypass limit and no cycle end-of-life percentage for these models
findings.source_title: Best 3000 Watt Portable Power Stations in 2026, RV Gear Lab (2026-10-02)
findings.note: Also read today: https://powerstationsrated.com/best-3000w-portable-power-station/ (16 models; watts not labelled continuous or surge) and https://wattsift.com/power-stations/best/3000w/ (TT-30 'not confirmed' for the F3000 and DELTA 3 Ultra). rvgearlab lists the Dabbsson 3000L as 3,000 W rated with a 3,600 W 'Power Boost' for compatible appliances only.

unsourced: Jackery HomePower 3000 from Jackery itself: today's price, ship notice, per-outlet ratings, cycle end-of-life percentage and cold derating (jackery.com returned HTTP 429 on three tries, via WebFetch and storecheck).

ALLPOWERS R3500: per-outlet and TT-30 ratings, cycle end-of-life percentage, weight (65.7 vs 93 lb) and the current price and cart total. The storecheck search on allpowers.com returned a non-JSON response and no R3500 page was opened.

BLUETTI Apex 200: the cycle count (the '6,000+' in our record is not in the page text read today, only the 70% basis), the amp rating of the 120 V outlets, the TT-30R watt rating, weight in lb, AC input watts and warranty years.

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus: a cycle-life figure from EcoFlow (its spec page lists none), and the bypass limit when plugged in. The manual PDF ChatGPT cited was downloaded but could not be converted to text in this session.
DJI Power 2000: per-outlet amp limit, outlet type, a rated output in watts for the US model (DJI gives 25 A only), surge watts, UPS switchover and today's US price.
Anker SOLIX F3000: today's price (sold out, 'Price Loading'), the end-of-life percentage behind '4000 Cycles', and the unit's warranty years.
EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra (non-Plus): whether it has a TT-30R and its per-outlet ratings; only the Ultra Plus port list was read.
Growatt HELIOS 3600, Mango Power E, Nature's Generator L3600 and Pecron F3000LFP: per-outlet ratings, cycle yardsticks and prices were not opened today.
A named reviewer's sustained 3,000 W load test, or a measured usable-Wh figure, for any candidate other than the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus and Ultra Plus.
